findings.title: Partial calibration has no post-diagnosis executor to publish its result index
findings.cause: The attempts maker must return and land before diagnosis. The admission interface assigns index authorship to the final measurement executor, while UNVERIFIED/OUT_OF_BAND and failed-revision branches can return without any final measurement call. No making call after diagnosis owns serialization of those returned findings and partial decision. An already closed attempts ticket cannot know later diagnostic findings, and the driver is explicitly restricted to deterministic export of already authored bytes.
findings.evidence: Source-derived partial branch at fixed ecd05f4117d4455afabca0638cfd9322b008e9f6: attempts do -> land/export -> diagnostic judge -> required gap or exhausted OUT_OF_BAND -> Return. references/admission/README.md:58-66 assigns the index exclusively to final measurement executor before closing and allows the driver only export.py. There is no index-making call on that reached branch. The new same-repository establish/land/export regression passes but only publishes synthetic attempt.json, never the later diagnostic/partial index.
findings.smallest_remedy: Add one ordinary same-repository record-finalization making step after the relevant diagnostic/qualification/measurement returns on every terminal branch, including no-final-measurement partials. Its sealed inputs are those actual returns and the selected decision; it commits the index and durable findings copies, then the driver exports the landed identity and probes. Do not reopen a sealed outcome or assign judgment/evidence authorship to role:none glue.

findings.title: Final probe requires retroactive mutation of already published round summaries
findings.cause: Each old round is recomputed using the final envelope revision_ledger, frozen_revision and final_record, then compared for whole-object equality. Those fields did not exist when the round was independently committed and exported. The new export boundary correctly refuses changed existing bytes, so following the durable-record contract makes later final/revision admission fail. The passing repair final fixture silently rewrites the old development summary.
findings.evidence: B1.1.10-reproductions.json / published_round_summary_must_be_rewritten_for_final: repaired final/development score-separation baseline passes CALIBRATED with final OUT_OF_BAND. Retaining summarize([development_record],development_policy) as originally published instead raises summary differs from recomputed evidence. Committing/exporting that original summary, then committing the future metadata rewrite required by probe makes actual export_records refuse external export differs: summary.json.
findings.smallest_remedy: Keep immutable round observations and their local snapshot metadata at their original identities. Recompute/compare each round against that snapshot, while the final aggregate index alone carries the accumulated revision ledger and frozen/final locators. Preserve development decision and final score separation. Exercise the actual temporal sequence with already exported old summaries; no retrospective rewrite or export overwrite should be required.

findings.title: The new per-call response can still be forged without solve or call completion
findings.cause: Moving expected values to the parent removes the literal outcome PASS injection, but the parent still trusts the complete per-call returned/value/exception/args_after object emitted through a file descriptor writable by candidate code. redirect_stdout does not restrict os.write(1,...). The candidate can exit before the harness checks its namespace or calls solve.
findings.evidence: B1.1.10-reproductions.json / new_call_protocol_spoof_without_api: the original outcome PASS print now correctly FAILs, and a real solve implementation PASSes. A source with no solve symbol executes os.write(1,b'{"returned":true,"value":7,"exception":null,"args_after":[3]}'); os._exit(0). Against the required solve(3)==7 case, actual grade returns PASS with empty failed_checks and exit 0. This is an updated semantic exploit of the changed interface, not the obsolete fixture.
findings.smallest_remedy: Establish actual callable/API execution and completion through a trusted boundary that candidate protocol writes or premature exit cannot impersonate. Add a candidate-writes-new-response negative control beside missing-API/old-PASS tests. If the chosen execution boundary cannot establish this property for the admitted source capabilities, return an explicit unsupported/UNVERIFIED instrument gap rather than accepting the forged call as evidence. Preserve legitimate Python call/exception/mutation behavior and do not claim host read isolation.

findings.title: Final attempts can be scored with substitute checks unrelated to the frozen benchmark
findings.cause: The repair now binds current package/frozen files to git, but check_attempt only checks the self-reported checks_locator and its matching hash, then replays that same file. It never resolves the expected case/grader input from the measured benchmark revision. Frozen bytes can stay intact while the actual evaluator silently uses a different external check file.
findings.evidence: B1.1.10-reproductions.json / final_attempt_grader_not_bound_to_frozen_checks: commit original solve(x)=x+1 checks in benchmark/checks.json and keep that exact frozen tree/inventory. The actual final candidate solve(x): return x FAILs those checks. Re-record the same native source against an uncommitted alternate external file expecting x, update the truthful local grader hash/observation and summary, and probe admits workflow/eligibility with final estimate 1.0. It reports the real fixed-check FAIL as a PASS measurement while every frozen byte remains unchanged.
findings.smallest_remedy: Bind each counted attempt case input and evaluator checks/required oracle to the named benchmark revision and declared case/split. Resolve or export those actual committed artifacts for scoring and verify any durable copy against that revision. For final attempts also bind the measured revision to the frozen identity. Reject substitute check files even when their self-reported hashes and replay outcomes agree; do not weaken complete-package or frozen-tree checks.

findings.title: Unavailable parent metadata bypasses a required nested configuration field
findings.cause: Required matching considers only whether the visited path equals or descends from a required path. An unavailable ancestor terminates recursion before reaching its required child. The final required-field loop checks only whether the requested field was absent, not whether the actual field is missing. A known requested child under an unavailable optional parent therefore produces only an optional gap.
findings.evidence: B1.1.10-reproductions.json / required_nested_field_hidden_by_unavailable_parent: requested scaffold.instructions=[pinned-instruction], resolved scaffold={unavailable_reason:parent object unavailable}, required_configuration_fields=[scaffold.instructions], band [1,1]. Both require_resolved_configuration=false and optional_configuration_fields=[scaffold] with global resolution=true return CALIBRATED and criterion_gaps []. Fully observed configuration correctly returns CALIBRATED.
findings.smallest_remedy: Evaluate every explicit required dotted path against resolved observations, including missing/unavailable ancestors; an optional ancestor or default cannot override a required descendant. Preserve optional gaps for unrelated fields and keep the legitimate fully observed branch passing.
